children.name: Casuarius
children.description: Large, flightless birds with a striking helmet-like casque on the head and brightly coloured wattled necks. They are solitary, frugivorous inhabitants of tropical rainforests and are considered keystone seed dispersers in New Guinea and northern Australia.

children.name: Casuarius casuarius
children.description: The southern cassowary (Casuarius casuarius), also known as double-wattled cassowary, Australian cassowary, or two-wattled cassowary, is a large, flightless, mostly black bird, found in Indonesia, Papua New Guinea, and northeastern Australia.

children.name: Casuarius unappendiculatus
children.description: The northern cassowary (Casuarius unappendiculatus), also known as the one-wattled cassowary, single-wattled cassowary, or golden-necked cassowary, is a large, stocky flightless bird of northern New Guinea.

children.name: Casuarius bennetti
children.description: The dwarf cassowary (Casuarius bennetti), also known as Bennett's cassowary, little cassowary, mountain cassowary or muruk, is the smallest of the three extant species of cassowaries.

children.name: Dromaius
children.description: A monotypic genus of the large, flightless emu, the second-tallest living bird after the ostrich. Highly adapted to the arid and variable conditions of the Australian continent.

children.name: Dromaius novaehollandiae
children.description: The emu (; Dromaius novaehollandiae) is a species of flightless bird endemic to Australia, where it is the tallest native bird.
